maria_g: Heads-up — after int4 bring-up for aurora-32k-magnet, we're seeing a small but consistent drift in outputs for long prefilled prompts (>= 8k tokens). Diff isn't catastrophic but reproducible across seeds. KV inspect shows a slow phase offset growing with distance, looks like a RoPE tilt/cascade. Anyone seen this pattern?

aj_carter: Can you paste minimal repro and a quick metric? e.g., L2 between logits or sample divergence?

maria_g: L2 between logits w/ fp16 vs int4: ~0.002 at 1k, ~0.012 at 8k, ~0.028 at 16k. Repro: run longprefill_repro.sh with sample prompt.

\maria_g: repro command: ```
# setup env 
python -m venv v && source v/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
python tests/longprefill_repro.py --model aurora-32k-int4 --prefill 16000 --seed 42 --dump-kv /tmp/kv_dump.npz
```

devon_ml: Interesting. Can you also dump rotary phase vectors (rot_cos/rot_sin) for a couple of layers? I suspect quant scale + index truncation is biasing the sin/cos alignment across shards.

maria_g: uploaded KV dump to s3://redwood-dev/kvdumps/1754321987/ (ping me for access). I included rot vectors for layers 2/10/24.

aj_carter: Quick thought: are we using the legacy wrap-around normalization in int4 path? There was a fix in runtime to do modular reduction per-block. If int4 uses different index math, RoPE index drift appears as a tilt. @eva_infra any runtime flag differences between int4 and fp16 rollout?

eva_infra: For int4 we enable quant_fast_path and index_stride_opt by default on dedicated nodes. There is a flag --rotary-wrap-check we can toggle to force canonical modular reduction and avoid accumulation. I'll run a canary with that flag off/on.

sanjay: Also worth checking KV cache eviction heuristics. If prefill strides got compacted differently under int4 mem layout, positions shifted by a constant offset would show as increasing phase residual. Could be a packing/padding mismatch.

maria_g: Good call. I re-ran with --rotary-wrap-check=on and observed L2 at 16k drop to ~0.011 (from 0.028). So flag helps a lot. But why only after ~4k tokens does it diverge?

devon_ml: That suggests a cascade: small index rounding error per-shard accumulates with sequence length. We should instrument per-token phase residual to confirm linear growth. I can add a quick hook in tests to compute phase_residual[token] = mean(abs(rot_fp16 - rot_int4)) across heads.

aj_carter: If it's linear, patching the index math is the right fix. But we should rule out KV packing. Maria — can you run the same repro but with contiguous shard layout (no compacted padding) to see if effect changes? Use --shard-layout=contiguous parameter.

maria_g: Running that now. ETA ~12m.

ci-bot: build/test job #3821 started: run-longprefill-repro (triggered by @maria_g). Logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/3821

ci-bot: build/test job #3821: step 'dump-kv' finished (12s). artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/3821/kv_dump.npz

maria_g: Result with contiguous layout: L2 at 16k = 0.013 (better than original 0.028 but slightly worse than --rotary-wrap-check on). So both KV packing and index reduction matter.

sanjay: OK that matches hypothesis: two orthogonal sources — packing induced position offset plus modular index reduction causing wrap mismatch. Combined they amplify.

devon_ml: Action plan: 1) add per-token phase residual logging to longprefill_repro, 2) run bisect between quant kernel versions (v1/v2) to see when delta introduced, 3) add unit test that asserts phase_residual < 0.005 up to 32k for canonical models.

aj_carter: +1. Also run a quick quality eval (QA prompts) with beam sampling to measure downstream LM quality drift (we care beyond L2). Maria, can you attach a small eval run?

maria_g: Ran quick QA eval (100 prompts) with greedy decode. Answer F1 drop: fp16 -> int4 = -0.9% overall, but top failures correlate with >0.02 phase residual on tail tokens. Uploaded eval report to the repro folder.

ci-bot: build/test job #3821 completed: PASS (4m 12s).

eva_infra: I'll open infra PR to enable --rotary-wrap-check by default on int4 pools and add a toggle in our Dedicated rollout. Also adding a small perf test to ensure no perf regression.

maria_g: I'll prepare a minimal regression test and the phase residual plot. Devon — can you handle the bisect on quant kernels?

devon_ml: Yep. I'll run bisect across kernel commits from last month. Expect ~2-3 hours. Will post findings here.

aj_carter: Great. If bisect points to kernel math, we can ship a microfix; otherwise we coordinate KV layout changes. Keep this thread for updates.

maria_g: Thanks all. Leaving reproducer and artifacts in s3 path. Next update after bisect or PR. :thumbsup:
